thread:
shreya: Heads-up — ACME Corp is seeing 429 bursts after last night's staged rate-policy change. They were on a 20% sample group and now report sustained errors. They say it started ~00:40 UTC.

mike: Copy. Which policy did we flip? Was this the per-project per-minute cap or the sliding window tweak?

shreya: We reduced per-project steady-state limit from 60 rps -> 45 rps and enabled burst-to-burst smoothing (window=30s). Canary was 20% traffic via rollout service. They included a bunch of request-ids.

lee: Quick check: gateway logs show 429s with header X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset in ~12s windows. Also seeing a spike in short-lived bursts (lots of small concurrent streams).

toni: Do we have autoscaler activity? Could be request patterns hitting reserved capacity thresholds and then queueing.

mike: Looking at infra — dedicated pool autoscaler did not trigger; CPU/GPU looks fine. This is purely policy churn at the gateway layer.

shreya: Customer repro steps they sent: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?project=acme-main
```
They posted multiple request-ids: req_akl2, req_z92q.

lee: Can we map those request-ids to the policy engine decision log? If we see the decision trace we can confirm whether the new limit applied.

mike: I pulled the decision logs for those ids: policy=project_rate_v3 sample_group=3 applied_limit=45 rps. It did apply.

shreya: ACME reports their client does short retries (1s backoff) on 429s which amplifies the sawtooth. They want either rollback or an immediate temporary exception for project=acme-main.

toni: We should avoid per-customer exceptions unless necessary. Proposal: quick rollback of staged change (undo rollout) to return to 60 rps while we investigate. Rollback window 10m, monitor 429 rate -> if <1% across their keys we hold. Agreed?

mike: +1. Steps: 1) pause rollout traffic (set sample weight 0) 2) revert policy to project_rate_v2 (60 rps) 3) verify headers and telemetry for 10 minutes. I can run the first two.

lee: I'll stand up an adhoc dashboard: 429 rate, X-RateLimit-Remaining distribution, request latency P95 for acme-main keys.

supportbot: [automated] alert #INC-2026-408 raised for acme-main 429 spike. Link: https://incidents/redwood/INC-2026-408

shreya: ACME gave approval for temporary rollback. They want us to notify once done and to provide request-ids to cross-check.

mike: Executing now: 
```
# pause rollout
./rolloutctl set-weight project_rate_v3 0 --env=prod
# rollback policy
./policyctl promote project_rate_v2 --env=prod
```

mike: Done. Set-weight returned OK, promote returned OK. Watching metrics.

lee: Dashboard shows 429 spike falling from 18% -> 2% within 90s. X-RateLimit-Remaining now >0 for most requests.

toni: Good. Support, please message ACME and confirm their traffic looks healthy. Also note this for postmortem: sampling group size too small to catch downstream retry amplification.

shreya: Messaged ACME: "we rolled back the change and are monitoring — please send any failing request-ids if you still see issues." They replied: "errors stopped after ~2m, thanks."

mike: Filing action items: 
- (mike) add a quick canary gating check to detect retry amplification (script: simulate N clients with short retries)
- (lee) expand canary telemetry to include X-RateLimit-Remaining percentiles and per-project retry counts
- (support) ensure ops runbook includes temporary exception flow (with security signoff)

toni: Also propose we increase initial canary to 30% for higher signal on burst patterns, but keep automatic rollback threshold conservative.

shreya: I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up with ACME and engineering to share timeline and next steps. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: Closing immediate rollback. We'll follow up with detailed postmortem and a small repro harness.

supportbot: [automated] incident INC-2026-408 acknowledged by mike at 1767000060

lee: Leaving a note: possible product change — update docs about client-side retry backoffs and how they interact with lower rate ceilings.

shreya: End-to-end done for now. Moving thread to #postmortems when we have RCA.
